threads.Author: codex
threads.Text: [Q] This four-event boundary is an inference from adjacent architectures, not validated user demand. Before planning implementation, pressure-test it against one real week-long delivery trace.
threads.SectionPath: Week-Long Human-Agent Implementation Alignment > Findings > F8 — the smallest seam is a reviewed projection of runtime events [Q2] [Q4]

Anchor.selected_text: Only four event classes have lasting planning value: milestone evidence, discovered deviation, blocking human decision, and completion summary.
Anchor.context_after: Routine progress, worker identity, retries, token usage, and logs remain runtime facts.

Replies.Author: codex
Replies.Text: Human direction from chat: the four-event projection is too thin by itself. Comments should provide a lightweight plan-derived work and status view that removes mental tracking, while still excluding workers, queues, retries, logs, and remote execution.

threads.Author: codex
threads.Text: [Q] This choice changes the product shape. A generic event input preserves runtime neutrality; a Codex-first adapter gives the fastest end-to-end dogfood. Which outcome matters more for the first proof?
threads.SectionPath: Week-Long Human-Agent Implementation Alignment > Open Questions

Anchor.selected_text: - First adapter: dogfood against Codex tasks, GitHub agent sessions, or a generic NDJSON event input?
Anchor.context_before: - Product fence: confirm that Comments never owns assignment, worker health, retries, scheduling, or remote execution.
Anchor.context_after: - Human surface: prefer status as anchored milestone threads, a generated read-only digest, or both?

Replies.Author: codex
Replies.Text: Human direction from chat: prioritize the OpenSpec-like lightweight artifact model and Factory-like emphasis on plan quality. The first proof should be native plan tracking and alignment status; runtime adapters can remain a later input surface.
Replies.SectionPath: Week-Long Human-Agent Implementation Alignment > Open Questions
